name: manual_10568f
claim: A dependency needed only to exercise cross-package compatibility in CI should not be published through any package metadata at all -- not project.dependencies, and not any [project.optional-dependencies] extra, since an optional extra is still published metadata that advertises a dependency relationship the package does not actually own. Install the compatibility fixture from a separate requirements file in a distinct CI step instead, keeping the package's own dependency declarations completely free of it

decisions.notes: 2026-09-13, oramasys/perpetua-core PR #6: this session's own first fix moved a test-only Agate dependency from dev into a distinctly-named optional-dependency group (test-agate-compat) inside pyproject.toml, reasoning that this kept dev genuinely test-tooling-only. A later commit on the same PR (89488880) established a stronger invariant: even a distinctly-named optional extra is still Core-published metadata implying a dependency relationship Core does not architecturally own. The final, adopted design moved the pin to requirements/test-agate-compat.txt entirely outside pyproject.toml, with CI installing it as a second, separate pip step -- and added a dedicated test (test_core_does_not_publish_agate_as_an_optional_dependency) specifically to prevent a future change from quietly reintroducing the dependency through an optional extra after removing it from required dependencies. General principle: package ownership and CI-environment composition are distinct authority surfaces, and a stronger, cleaner invariant is worth adopting even after a working, weaker one already exists. Full write-up: .agent/memory/working/PERPETUA_CORE_PR6_RECOVERY_ARCHITECTURE_AND_REVIEW_LESSONS_2026-09-13.md.
